ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast bimodal distribution. Visible white-to-light-grey pixels occupy approximately 65% of the visible surface area, while dark-grey-to-black pixels occupy approximately 35%, concentrated at the center and lower margins.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Central region spanning the peduncle connection to the median notch is dominated by a solid black contiguous mass. This dark pigmentation extends along the lower leading edges. The mid-to-outer lobes feature white dominant backgrounds with fine dark speckling and irregular black mottling concentrated along the trailing edges and lower quadrants of the left lobe.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with an approximate internal angle of 35 degrees; depth is significant, creating two distinct lobes with a sharp interior convergence point.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations are present along the entire trailing edge of both lobes. Serrations exhibit pixel-amplitude variations ranging from shallow undulations to sharp, tooth-like peaks, particularly prominent on the inner half of the right lobe.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: The trailing edge follows a concave curve from the median notch extending outward to the distal tips, terminating in sharp, upward-curving points.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density, 3D-protruding clusters of white-to-cream circular barnacle colonies (Coronula diadema) are present on both the far left and far right distal tips of the fluke.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several high-contrast white linear marks are visible on the right lobe. One prominent near-vertical abrasion is located approximately midway between the notch and the right tip, with smaller, unaligned scratches scattered across the lower right lobe surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive barnacle colonization on the distal tips causing significant alteration of the edge profile. Possible minor indentation or notch on the outer left edge just below the primary barnacle cluster.
other_distinctive_markers: The vertical white rake mark on the right lobe is a highly distinct identifier, along with the specific density and spatial arrangement of the barnacle clusters on the fluke tips.
